#2631. Luka Dončić points, reaction as Lakers take on Hornets

The Los Angeles Lakers (13-2) got their ninth straight win, but it took everything to get past the Charlotte Hornets (4-10) in a 118-114 overtime thriller on Tuesday, Nov. 17. With both Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler ruled out ahead of tipoff, it looked like the onus would fall on Luka Dončić's ability to continue his historic start to the season, but it was Quentin Grimes who emerged as the hero of the night while Dončić had a pedestrian (by his standards) 36 points.

Dončić found himself in foul trouble early when he got whistled for his fourth in the final seconds before halftime, and the Hornets led by as many as 18 points in the third before a 7-2 run to end the quarter put the Lakers back within striking distance of a 13-point deficit.

With Dončić on the bench for the first six minutes of the final frame, Grimes went nuclear for 21 points, capping off the Lakers' rally with a last-second 3 – on an assist from Dončić – to force OT. The 26-year-old wing finished the night with a career-high 47 points on another career-high 10 threes made, making him the only Laker aside from Kobe Bryant to score at least 10 shots from long range.

Dončić, meanwhile, got his 11th consecutive 30-point game to continue his historic early season tear. Despite the fouls and some brutal turnovers in the first half, he finished the night with seven assists and six rebounds, including some key defensive boards and takeaways down the stretch.

Grimes and Dončić combined for 83 points and 15 threes as the Lakers outscored the Hornets 37-20 over the fourth quarter and overtime; within that stretch, Charlotte was held to just three points in OT.

Through 12 games played entering Tuesday, Dončić was leading the NBA with 39.0 points per game, 7.8 assists and 7.2 rebounds while shooting 48.6% from the field and a career-best 40.6% from 3-point range. He's coming off a 43-point performance in Sunday's win over the Phoenix Suns, his seventh game scoring at least 40. With Dončić on the floor, the Lakers have outscored their opponents by a total of 115 points.

His defense has also been spectacular, averaging 2.4 steals in LA's active eight-game win streak. The 27-year-old's four charges drawn are second-most in the league; he's also tied for third in defensive loose balls recovered (eight) this season.

USA TODAY Sports provided updates and highlights of the Lakers vs. Hornets game:

Quentin Grimes put his fingerprints all over this one. Aside from his career-high 47-point game and forcing overtime, the wing disrupted Charlotte's inbound pass to Royce O'Neale to force what ended up being the turnover that decided the game. The Lakers got the ball back up one with 17.5 seconds left, and the Hornets quickly fouled Grimes to send him to the line, where he hit both free throws to put LA up by three.

Matisse Thybulle forced another turnover on the ensuing possession and made a free throw to give the Lakers a two-possession lead -- and the win.

The Lakers have their first lead since the second quarter on a fadeaway from Dončić at the 3:15 mark of the overtime period.

It was only fitting for the hot hand to save LA's win-streak at the last second. Matisse Thybulle grabbed a missed Coby White free throw and fed it to Luka Dončić, who made his way to the three-point line but ultimately found Grimes on the opposite wing.

It was Grimes' 10th made three of the night, and at 45 points he's now one shy of his career-high.

Dončić reaps the rewards of Grimes' hot hand in the fourth, completing the rally with a three of his own to tie the game at 104-all with just over three minutes to go. The shot puts Dončić at 32 points on the night, his 11th consecutive 30-point game.

Elgin Baylor is the only other Lakers with multiple streaks of at least 11 consecutive 30-point games.

This is supposed to be a Luka Dončić live blog, but it's Grimes who has taken over with the Slovenian superstar on the bench halfway through the fourth quarter. Grimes continues his hot streak from Sunday, and has now hit 8-of-10 threes -- tying his career-high -- and has scored 13 points in the quarter to reach 37 points. It's Grimes' ninth career 30-point game.

The Lakers now trail by just four, and Dončić has checked back into the game.

It's been a rough night for LA. Luka Dončić is up to 29 points but went cold shooting 1-for-5 over the final six minutes of the frame, the lone bucket a floater at the 46-second mark. The Hornets have led by as many as 18 but a 7-2 run to close the quarter has put the Lakers back within striking distance.

Dončić returned to the floor at his usual time despite the early foul trouble, and that risk worked out early on as he went off for 13 points in the second quarter... until he got whistled for shoving Royce O'Neale coming up the court with eight seconds to go before halftime for his fourth foul of the game. JJ Redick voiced his displeasure at the call and picked up a technical in the process.

The Lakers trail the Hornets 66-59 at the half after an impressive showing from Brandon Miller and Naz Reid, who have 19 points apiece and have led Charlotte -- the worst shooting team in the league at 40% entering Tuesday -- to a 54.8% field goal percentage through the first two frames.

Dončić has 22 points, four assists and two rebounds. Quentin Grimes has 16 points and has made four of his five three-pointers, but they're the only two Lakers in double figures at halftime. Matisse Thybulle (six points) is the only other Laker with more than four points.

It's been a frustrating first quarter for the Lakers superstar, who scored just four points through the first 10 minutes of the opening frame as Sion James has been playing suffocating defense. Dončić managed to get five points in the final two minutes before he was called for a charge on James on the Lakers' second-to-last possession. Head coach JJ Redick challenged the call, but the ruling was upheld due to an off-arm shove from Dončić.

Dončić finished the quarter with nine points shooting just 33.3% and is one of six from deep as the Lakers trail Charlotte 34-30. He usually sits the first six minutes of the second quarter, but Redick has a decision to make as he now has to manage his best player's foul troubles with his second and third best players both out.

Fox's Sunday tripleheader culminated in the national telecast of the 8-1 49ers at the record-doesn't-matter Cowboys.

#2629. Gilbert Arenas claims ‘heartless’ Klay Thompson’s Megan Thee Stallion breakup led to resurgence

Klay Thompson is finding himself delivering at a level many fans got accustomed to during his prime with the Golden State Warriors.

Earlier this year, Thompson ended his relationship with rapper Megan Thee Stallion, which became quite a pop culture controversy.

And given how well Thompson is playing since joining the Miami Heat, Gilbert Arenas believes the breakup has helped him find his form again.

Speaking on The Arena show, Gilbert Arenas spoke about Klay Thompson's recent return to form from a shooting standpoint.

Arenas suggests that the nature and fallout of his recent breakup with rapper Megan Thee Stallion has somehow given him the confidence he needs to once again become the elite shooter he once was.

"One of the greatest shooters of all time not having his shot, when that's what you do for a living… Sometimes, certain type of minds need certain things," Arenas said. "I think the Megan Thee Stallion (situation), just watching someone like, 'this is the worst break-up I've ever had,' made him sleep good at night. The old Klay is back!"

"Sometimes, in the movie, that killer has a soft spot, and he's more vulnerable… He just lost his touch. When he'd seen that, and she was all distraught, he probably sat back like, 'Yeah. This is me. When they're crying at the doorstep, my shot is back!'

"I just really believe that's all it took. Looking at the phone, talking about, 'I hate your guts,' and he's thinking, 'Yeah, I'm about to have 30 tonight!' Everything is back.

"Klay is back! The killer is back! Keep shooting the ball, baby, and keep breaking hearts! You've got to add that part to it. He shoots like he's heartless! Gotta keep breaking hearts!"

This season, Thompson is averaging 15.5 points, 2.1 assists, and 1.4 rebounds, while shooting 45.1% from the field and 43.4% from beyond the arc.

Thompson has hit 50+ three-pointers in just 13 games this season, the fastest he has reached this mark at any point in his NBA career.

#2627. LaMelo Ball's steal sets up Wolves' go-ahead layup, then Trey Lyles makes game-saving block vs. Trail Blazers

While starring for the Charlotte Hornets, LaMelo Ball was far too often a defensive liability. The 25-year-old guard isn't even a month into his first regular season with the Minnesota Timberwolves, and they're already squeezing significantly more effort out of him on that end of the court.

That uptick in defensive intensity helped deliver the Wolves a 106-105 victory on Tuesday night at home against the Portland Trail Blazers.

With 8.1 seconds remaining, and Minnesota trailing by one point, Ball got a piece of an inbounds pass from Portland's Donovan Clingan, poking it free. Wolves guard Ayo Dosunmu corralled the loose ball and flipped on the accelerator. Rather than attacking the paint on a night he scored a season-high 30 points, the guard fired a pass down low to forward Jaden McDaniels, who quickly dropped in the go-ahead layup with 2.6 ticks to go.

With his team suddenly down one, Clingan connected on his next inbounds pass, as the big man hit star guard Damian Lillard in stride. Except Lillard's drive was denied by an elevating Trey Lyles. The 6-foot-9 veteran rejected the shot out of bounds.

Portland got one last chance with a second remaining on the clock. Robert Williams III couldn't handle the lob from Clingan; however, the ball ended up with Toumani Camara, whose last-second attempt was contested by Ball in the paint and off the mark.

Ball let out a triumphant roar as the buzzer sounded. He finished with 18 points on 7-of-17 shooting, but his defense down the stretch was pivotal. As for Lyles, he chipped in 8 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists and that game-saving block in 31 minutes off the bench.

McDaniels' final basket gave him 22 points. He had a team-high three steals.

Altogether, the Timberwolves (11-4) held off a Trail Blazers (9-5) team that was fueled by a combined 48 points from Lillard (25) and his backcourt partner, Jrue Holiday (23).

Minnesota currently leads the NBA in defensive rating. It is in the top 10 of that category for the fifth straight season. This time around, Ball is part of that display, adopting the Wolves' defensive DNA.

#2625. Waterford heading to boys soccer CIAC final for first time since 1987

DEEP RIVER - Waterford boys soccer coach Jeff Emerich was grooving when he heard "Jump" by Kris Kross hip-hopping over the Valley Regional PA at halftime of Tuesday night's CIAC Class M semifinal between his No. 1-seeded Lancers and No. 5 Daniel Hand.

Emerich knew, too, that if his boys executed a little more criss-cross on the pitch, they'd be jumping Waterford boys soccer into a state final for the first time since 1987, about five years before Chris "Mac Daddy" Kelly and Chris "Daddy Mac" Smith arrived on the scene.

Yeah, it all goes back a ways, and it's funny what stands the test of time.

This Waterford boys soccer team of 2026 is proving to be one for the ages. With a 2-0 victory over Hand on Tuesday night, in a game that showcased the breadth of their remarkable skill set, the Lancers are one step away from the first-ever boys soccer championship in Waterford history.

Brady Wiseman scored off a left-side cross from Brayden Michonski two minutes into the second half and Jaydev Villa, set up by an inexorable upfield rush by Yaman Qarqour, added insurance with 20:35 to play as Waterford improved to 19-1-1 and advances to this weekend's state championship at Trinity Health Stadium in Hartford to face No. 2 Weston, which dethroned reigning champ Tolland 1-0 in Tuesday's other Class M semi.

"It's been since 1987 since the last time we made it in, so this is our first chance to go up and compete," Emerich said. "We've never won a state title, and it's been 39 years since we've seen a chance, so we are very humbled that we are able to do this, and we continue to work, and that's the thing that makes these boys special."

The Lancers got an emotional boost on Monday when they learned goalie Luke Wilson was cleared from a concussion suffered in the ECC tournament semifinals against Bacon Academy. Wilson set the tone Tuesday night by charging out and sliding to break up a Hand scoring chance in the opening minute for the first of his 16 saves.

"I didn't even know if I was going to be able to play this game, especially last week, watching when we played Lewis Mills (in the quarterfinals), I was still nervous," Wilson said. "All I wanted to do was get back on the field."

Wilson wore a foam helmet for the first time Tuesday night. The rest was very much the same look for a Waterford team that has now scored 94 goals and allowed just 13 on the season.

The first half was fairly even, with both teams generating scoring chances. In the second half, the pitch decidedly tilted Waterford's way. Once Wiseman converted that cross from Michonski, a stiff challenge for Hand grew steeper. The Tigers, the last SCC team in the boys soccer state tourney, ended their season at 16-5-1.

"I thought our team came out and executed our game plan in the first half really, really well," said Hand coach Mike Shirley. "It was always going to be a game decided by one-versus-one moments, and we knew we had to defend them on the edges, and it was just about, 'Can we find our opportunities and put them in the back of the net before they can?'"

The Tigers could not, and with it passed their chance to return to the state finals for the first time since the grand slam championship run of 2016-2019.

Dates and times for all state soccer finals will be announced later this week.

Luke Wilson. Cleared from a concussion just one day before the game, Waterford's senior goalie opened the night with a sliding, charging stop to thwart a Hand scoring chance and punctuated the victory punching out a final shot in the final minute. Wilson had 16 saves in all.

#2622. Greenwich holds off Ridgefield for 4th straight Class LL girls swimming title, 33rd overall

WEST HARTFORD - The Greenwich and Ridgefield girls swimming and diving programs have engaged in plenty of battles over the years, and the CIAC Class LL championship meet on Tuesday night at the Cornerstone Aquatics Center was no different.

For the Cardinals, depth turned out to be key as they captured their fourth straight Class LL title and 33rd overall in program history. Greenwich scored 924 points to second-place Ridgefield's 878.5. Amity was third with 510.5 points.

"I felt pretty confident going into this because I knew that everyone on the team has been working super hard, and I had a lot of faith in us," Greenwich junior Olivia DeVries said.

With sophomore Alden Charette's first-place finish in Class LL diving, the Cardinals won three individual events and one relay. Seniors Kensie Worden (50 freestyle, 23.59) and Julia Kozma (100 butterfly, 57.70) won gold medals, as did the opening 200 medley relay team of Charette, junior Sara Jee, Kozma and Worden (1:47.96).

Greenwich claimed 18 individual medals, including three golds, three silvers and three bronzes. DeVries claimed bronze medals in the 200 freestyle and 500 freestyle.

"I'm super proud of the team because we all have worked so hard in practice. The captains have done such a good job to keep us motivated and I'm just very proud of how hard we worked," DeVries said. "Every single swimmer made a difference, every single spot. If you were in the C final, the A final, everyone makes a difference. We are all cheering for each other, and I think that's what makes Greenwich special."

"We had some really great swims from all the girls, but especially our senior class," Greenwich coach Megan Kelly said. "I think it really means a lot to them, and to see them swim with such heart was really great."

Senior Ellison Charette was second in the 200 IM and 500 freestyle, and she was part of the second-place 200 and 400 freestyle relay teams.

"Ellison, she fought hard in both of her races. She had some really good swims. Overall, I was really, really pleased," Kelly said. "They didn't win the (200) free relay, but they went 1:35, which is All-American consideration time. That was pretty impressive."

Greenwich's second-place 200 freestyle relay finished in 1:35.79. Ridgefield's first-place relay of sophomore Zsofia Milak, senior Dalia Katra, sophomore Mary Kelly and junior Ellie Griffin swam the race in 1:35.21, which broke Ridgefield's 2022 state record of 1:35.48.

Milak had a terrific night for Ridgefield, winning individual gold medals in the 200 freestyle (1:50.20) and 100 freestyle (50.95). She was also part of the first-place 400 freestyle relay (3:32.60), along with Kelly, junior Chloe Archibald and sophomore Charlie Palmer. Kelly won the 500 freestyle in 4:59.44.

Norwalk/McMahon junior standout Emma Giafardino won gold medals in the 200 IM (2:05.71) and 100 breaststroke (1:04.71). Trumbull sophomore Noelle Ivanovich won the 100 backstroke in 57.47.

Greenwich and Ridgefield will likely be the top contenders Sunday for the State Open at Yale.

"I think across the board there were some really great swims. It was a battle though, and it's always fun to have a battle," Megan Kelly said. "We had it at FCIACs, now we've had it here, and Opens is going to be another battle. It makes it a lot more fun this way."

#2621. 2026 MLB Rookie of the Year: Tigers' Kevin McGonigle, Reds' Sal Stewart win BBWAA awards

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Kevin McGonigle of the Tigers and Sal Stewart of the Reds were named the 2026 Rookies of the Year in their respective leagues on Monday night as part of the BBWAA's awards week. McGonigle earned 28 of 30 first-place votes, beating out the Guardians' Parker Messick and the Red Sox's Payton Tolle. Stewart, meanwhile, beat the Mets' Carson Benge and the Cardinals' JJ Wetherholt.

Because McGonigle and Stewart were both with the major-league team for long enough to earn a full year of service time, the Tigers and Reds will each receive a Prospect Promotion Incentive pick in the 2027 MLB Draft.

The annual awards, which also include Manager of the Year, Reliever of the Year, Cy Young and MVP, are voted on by 30 members of the Baseball Writers Association of America (that's two per MLB city in each league). Votes were submitted before the beginning of the playoffs, meaning that only regular-season contributions are taken into account.

Stewart won the battle of Old School stats vs. New School stats here. Though he only posted 2.0 WAR, he had 32 home runs and 111 RBI, putting him in rarefied air for a rookie. He's one of just 15 rookies ever with at least 30 homers and 100 RBI. The only names from that list to not win the award either faced another player from the list or played before Rookie of the Year was awarded. Everyone else has taken home the hardware, just as Stewart did Monday evening.

Overall, Stewart appeared in all 162 games, hitting .263/.330/.457 (117 OPS+) with 25 doubles, 32 homers, 112 RBI, 87 runs and 15 steals.

Stewart earned 20 of the 30 available first-place votes.

Carson Benge of the Mets finished second and JJ Wetherholt of the Cardinals finished in third place. Benge, the 2024 first-rounder, made the team out of spring training and hit .282/.346/.430 with 20 home runs, 22 steals and 4.3 WAR. Defensive metrics love Wetherholt and helped push him to 4.5 WAR in 139 games. He hit .242/.339/.365 with 17 homers, 14 steals and 89 runs.

Stewart joins the following Reds as Rookie of the Year winners:

The honor for McGonigle completes a stellar year for the former first-round draft pick. He broke camp with the Tigers and was productive from the get-go. He ended up hitting .278/.376/.430 (126 OPS+) with 28 doubles, five triples, 18 home runs, 72 RBI, 97 runs, 12 steals and 7.1 WAR, the latter good enough for the AL lead among position players. He played great defense, ran the bases well and was an All-Star. He nearly walked (95) as much as he struck out (100), too. Not much more could've been asked of the Pennsylvania native who played most of the season at age 21, and he's a well-deserving Rookie of the Year.

A few weeks after he debuted, he and the team agreed to an eight-year, $150 million extension.

McGonigle won in a blowout, getting 28 of the 30 available first-place votes, scoring 204 of a possible 210 points.

He joins the following players who have won the award with the Tigers:

Parker Messick of the Guardians finishes second after going 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA, 1.06 WHIP and 193 strikeouts in 186 ⅓ innings; he is also a top-three finalist for the Cy Young award. Red Sox starter Payton Tolle finishes third after going 9-6 with a 3.03 ERA (135 ERA+), 1.10 WHIP and 171 strikeouts in 148 ⅔ innings.

#2619. Bob Boone, All-Star catcher, 1980 World Series champion and father of Yankees manager, dies at 78

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Bob Boone, a four-time All-Star catcher and the middle member of a three-generation baseball family, has died. He was 78. His son, Bret Boone, made the announcement on Tuesday. No cause of death was given.

My dad- He was my mentor, my coach, my rock. He taught me how to be a pro and more importantly, how to be a man. He was one of the highest integrity people I’ve ever known and I’m going to miss him dearly. Baseball lost a great one yesterday. R.I.P dad, I love you❤️ pic.twitter.com/4NtYAwXIv3

"Bob Boone had an enduring impact on the field as a 19-year MLB veteran, a seven-time Gold Glove Award-winning catcher, a four-time All-Star and 1980 World Champion with the Philadelphia Phillies," the MLB Players Association said in a statement. "He embraced a leadership role in the Players Association early in his career, and earned a reputation as a strong and principled voice in the advancement of player rights in the 1970s and '80s ... As we honor Bob's legacy and mourn his passing, we extend our heartfelt condolences to his wife, Sue, sons Aaron, Bret and Matt, his extended family, and his many fans and admirers throughout the game."

The Boones were baseball's first three-generation family. Bob's father, Ray Boone, played for six teams from 1948-60, and his sons Aaron and Bret both had long careers spanning the 1990s and 2000s. Bob's other son, Matt, played in the minor leagues.

"I'm just so grateful that I had a dad that took us to work with him all the time," Aaron, now manager of the New York Yankees, said in 2023 (via MLB.com). "He came up at the end of '72, and I was born in the spring of '73. He played until my senior year in high school and literally I was at the ballpark -- my brothers and I, in unis, shagging (fly balls) and doing everything you could possibly imagine. It was a great way to grow up."

Born in San Diego, Bob Boone made his MLB debut with the Phillies in 1972 and took over as the club's starting catcher in 1973. He hit 10 home runs and finished third in the National League Rookie of the Year voting. That started a 17-year run as one of the game's best and most durable catchers. Boone started at least 130 games behind the plate eight times in his career and 110 games 14 times.

With the Phillies in 1980, Boone went 7 for 17 (.412) with four walks and zero strikeouts in Philadelphia's six-game World Series win over the Kansas City Royals.

A seven-time Gold Glove winner, including four straight during his age-38 to -41 seasons, Boone had his most productive years with the Phillies from 1976-79. He hit .282/.351/.414 those four seasons and averaged nine home runs, which was excellent output given the offensive standard at the catcher position during that era. Boone went to four All-Star Games and received MVP votes twice.

"Bob was an incredible player, teammate and family man," the Phillies said in a statement. "He embodied everything we believe exemplary athletes should represent, both on and off the field. We were proud to have him as part of the Phillies family during one of the most historic runs in team history. His impact on our organization, his teammates, and everyone who had the privilege of knowing him will never be forgotten."

Boone ranks second with 2,161 games at catcher during the Modern Era (since 1900), behind only Hall of Famer Ivan Rodriguez (2,377). He is 15th among primary catchers with 1,838 hits and 21st with 2,508 total bases. Boone played parts of 19 big league seasons with the Phillies (1972-81), California Angels (1982-88), and Royals (1989-90).

The Orlando SunRays, a potential expansion franchise, hired Boone to be their manager soon after he retired as a player, though the expansion franchises were instead awarded to Denver and Miami in 1991. Boone later managed the Royals from 1995-97 and the Cincinnati Reds (2001-03). He managed his son, Aaron, those years with the Reds.

In 2005, Boone joined the Washington Nationals as their director of player development and had a hand in building the core that won the franchise's first World Series title in 2019. He remained with the Nationals until 2021. Boone spent five years on the Hall of Fame ballot from 1996 to 2000 but was not voted into Cooperstown.

#2618. No. 10 Illinois' Stojakovic goes for 46 points, sets scoring mark by opponent on Duke's home floor

DURHAM, N.C. (AP) — Over and over again, Andrej Stojakovic stared down a would-be defender, put the ball on the floor and slipped past on his way to attacking the paint.

He finished on fadeaways and drives to the rim. Got to the foul line. And by the end, Stojakovic had not only led 10th-ranked Illinois to a surprisingly one-sided win against No. 5 Duke, but he had also scored the most points ever by an opponent in the Blue Devils' famously rowdy home gym.

The 6-foot-7 senior finished with 46 points in Tuesday night's 99-78 win, breaking a record that had stood for nearly seven decades while helping the Illini end Duke's 35-game winning streak at Cameron Indoor Stadium. It was part of a jarring overall performance by the Fighting Illini, both for Stojakovic's own brilliance and the way it left Blue Devils coach Jon Scheyer flummoxed by his team's lack of competitive fight.

"Just finding a rhythm, staying aggressive the whole time," Stojakovic said as he leaned against a wall in a cramped hall outside of Duke's visiting locker room. "My teammates believed in me from the start. I think credit to them for sticking with it.

"That's the beauty of this team. There's no ego on this team. And it could be anybody's night."

Maybe so, but there's no questioning whose night this really was.

The son of three-time NBA All-Star Peja Stojakovic had 20 by halftime on the way to finishing 14 of 21 from the field and 16 of 20 from the foul line. That allowed him to surpass the previous scoring record by a Duke opponent here: 43 points, set by South Carolina's Grady Wallace in February 1957.

Stojakovic also came within two points of matching Duke's Dick Groat (48 in February 1952) for the most points by any player in Cameron's nearly 87-year history.

A week earlier, the Illini didn't respond to a hostile road environment in a loss at now-No. 9 Texas Tech. Stojakovic said the Illini treated this one as a must-win opportunity in how they prepared. That included his own homework of studying Duke's top defenders for tendencies.

Then he went out and dictated how this marquee nonconference matchup would play out.

"Honestly, that's what he is, that's who he is every day," said freshman Quentin Coleman, who had 27 points as the second half of a 1-2 punch. "He's a scorer, and when he goes down and scores, I don't think anybody can stop him. He just had one of those nights, and we just fed him the ball — and he just led us."

Incredibly, Stojakovic pumped out those points without relying on the 3-point shot (2 for 3), instead going with a mix of never-rushed offensive efficiency and a degree of old-fashioned attacking edge.

It was attacking in transition against Duke big man Patrick Ngongba II for a scooping layup. Elevating over a flat-footed Dame Sarr — Duke's top perimeter defender — to bury a first-half 3-pointer, then following moments later by getting John Blackwell backpedaling into the paint before turning to knock down a fadeaway.

"He's a great player, he got it going," Sarr said, "and I didn't stop him."

It was part of what coach Brad Underwood noted was an offensive performance without relying on the ball screens that helped free freshman guard and eventual No. 5 overall NBA draft pick Keaton Wagler for 46 points at Purdue last year. Rather, Underwood said, Stojakovic and his teammates simply "hunted matchups and opportunities."

Stojakovic offered tough-nosed plays too, like when he missed a muscled-up shot against Sarr — but outfought Sarr and Ngongba to the rebound and scored while being fouled for a basket that had the Illinois bench roaring in approval.

"I hope he continues to like those things," Underwood said. "That's what we've been trying to get him to do. That's nasty. There's nastiness in that play, an aggression in that play."

Stojakovic finally checked out at the 1:22 mark with victory in hand, greeted by a rousing cheer from the orange-clad Illini fans packed into Cameron's bleachers behind the visiting bench and a hug from Underwood.

Across the court, that image was also a capper to a performance that Blackwell said had left him "in shock a little bit."

Scheyer credited Stojakovic for an "all-time" performance in Duke's first home loss since falling to rival North Carolina in March 2024 to end the regular season. But he was also critical of his own team's response in this marquee nonconference matchup.

Worse, this one came a week after Duke got pushed around against another Big Ten team in a loss to now-No. 2 Michigan State.

"All I would tell you guys is this is not the team we're going to put on the floor," Scheyer said. "The lack of competing that we did tonight and the lack of connectivity, we're going to fix and we're going to work like crazy.

"We may lose some games this year, but we're not going to lose where we don't compete."

I hate to get so negative just one week into the season, but the Philadelphia Flyers have forced my hand. After a magical run to the second round of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Flyers have fallen on their face through four games.

#2616. MLB rumors: Mets to meet with Tarik Skubal, Rangers' Corey Seager plan, plus Blue Jays, Cubs, Red Sox, more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

This is an important week on the baseball calendar. First and foremost, it is awards week. Kevin McGonigle and Sal Stewart were named the Rookies of the Year on Monday. The Managers of the Year will be announced Tuesday, Cy Youngs and Relievers of the Year will be announced Wednesday, and finally the MVPs will be announced Thursday.

Also, the GM Meetings are this week in Las Vegas. The GM Meetings are not the Winter Meetings in terms of the sheer volume of rumors and transactions, but they do usually provide some news. There could be more than usual this year given the near certainty of a lockout on Dec. 1, which would also mean there are no Winter Meetings. This may be the only time everyone is in the same room this winter. The three weeks between now and Dec. 1 could be quite active.

We've already ranked the top 50 free agents and the top 25 trade candidates.

With that in mind, here are Tuesday's hot stove rumors.

The Mets have a meeting scheduled with two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, the clear top free agent avaiable this offseason, later this week, reports the New York Post. Skubal will meet with teams in California, presumably at the offices of agent Scott Boras. Owner Steve Cohen is expected to push for Skubal, according to SNY; president of baseball operations David Stearns has long been reluctant to sign big-money, long-term deals for pitchers, though pitchers of Skubal's caliber are rarely available. The Mets are also seeking first base help and bullpen reinforcements.

Nolan McLean and Christian Scott are the only locks for New York's 2027 rotation at the moment. Justin Hagenman, Sean Manaea, Kodai Senga, Zac Thornton, and Jonah Tong are next in line to make starts. Tylor Megill is expected back from Tommy John surgery early next year as well. The Mets have some depth but clearly need more impact.

The Rangers signed Corey Seager to a 10-year, $325 million deal prior to the 2022 season and it paid off quite handsomely with a World Series title in 2023 (Seager was the World Series MVP). With five years and roughly $155 million left on the deal, however, the Rangers appear ready to trade him.

The Rangers "intend to explore moving Seager at the general managers' meetings," reports The Athletic.

Seager, 32, was stellar from 2023 to 2025 in spite of a litany of injuries, averaging 6.2 WAR per season with a .294 average and 158 OPS+. He actually averaged 8.7 WAR per 162 games. Only the injuries kept him from making multiple serious MVP runs. Last season, though, was a step back. In 102 games, he hit .227/.312/.424 with 20 home runs, 51 RBI and 3.1 WAR.

The injury history keeps getting more extensive, too, as he's dealt with injuries to his thumb, hamstring, hip, other hamstring and back in the last four years.

With a lackluster, at best, shortstop class in free agency, now might be the perfect time for the Rangers to move on from Seager, assuming a deal can be worked out with the years and dollars left on his contract. Texas also has Sebastian Walcott, one of the top prospects in baseball, ready in the wings.

The Blue Jays are among the teams with interest in free agent second baseman Brandon Lowe, according to Sportsnet. Ernie Clement, Toronto's primary second baseman in 2026, crashed hard in the second half and has always fit better as a super utility man who plays regularly at different positions. Josh Smith is the team's other second base option.

Lowe would bring needed power to a team that finished dead last in home runs this past season and had just one player, Kazuma Okamoto (33), clear 15 home runs. Only four Blue Jays hit even 10 homers. Also, Toronto's lineup is mostly right-handed. Lowe would add power and also a lefty bat to provide balance. We ranked him as the 13th-best free agent available.

Adding rotation help is a "top priority," White Sox GM Chris Getz said during an MLB Network Radio interview on Tuesday. "We're going to exhaust the starter market, both free agency -- we'll take a look -- along with trades. That is our top priority," Getz said. He also confirmed that Grant Taylor, the team's postseason closer, will move into the rotation. Hagen Smith will remain in the bullpen.

The White Sox have solid enough rotation depth with Taylor joining Sean Burke, Luis Castillo, Anthony Kay, Davis Martin, David Sandlin, Noah Schultz, and perhaps Shane Smith and Drew Thorpe. There is room for improvement, though, particularly at the top. Chicago could use a bona fide ace, not that one is easy to acquire or abundantly available.

Add the Padres to the list of teams that have shown interest in Skubal, reports MLB Network. San Diego has a major need in the rotation -- Joe Musgrove, who hasn't made a start since the 2024 postseason, and Randy Vásquez are their only rotation locks -- and a new ownership group that seems willing to spend in its first offseason.

Skubal is far and away the offseason's best free agent. He is also a Scott Boras client, and, historically, top Boras clients take the largest contract offer regardless of team situation. That isn't to say the Padres are a bad situation. Not at all. They're a very good team that is in the postseason most years, plus they play in San Diego. Who doesn't love San Diego?

The Padres are also connected to several Japanese players, according to The Athletic. That includes MLB free agents Seiya Suzuki and Shota Imanaga, as well as players coming over from Nippon Professional Baseball, like third baseman Teruaki Sato.

Free agent lefty Adrian Morejon is drawing interest as a starting pitcher, but he prefers to remain in the bullpen, according to The Athletic. Even during the season, there were rumblings that Morejon would like to be given a chance to start in 2027. He came up through the minors as a starter and only remained in the bullpen because he was so dominant in a late-inning role.

We ranked Morejon as the offseason's second-best free agent on the idea that he would move into the rotation. The belief within the game is that he has a chance to be an excellent starter, not just a back-end piece. Either way, Morejon is a very good pitcher, and at 28, he's also one of the youngest free agents available. He should have several peak years remaining.

Although they are disinclined to pursue Tarik Skubal, the Cubs hope to add three established starting pitchers this offseason, reports The Athletic. Of the nine pitchers to make at least nine starts for Chicago in 2027, seven are free agents. Only Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery (per ESPN), and Edward Cabrera, who had a 5.96 ERA and was demoted to the bullpen, remain.

Left-hander Justin Steele is expected back from UCL surgery next year, though he suffered a setback this summer and wasn't able to return as hoped in September. Others like Javier Assad and Jordan Wicks are depth options more than full-time rotation pieces. This free agent class offers plenty of second- and third-tier starters. That's where the Cubs are expected to shop.

Unlike last offseason, the Mets are not interested in a major overhaul despite their disappointing year, reports MLB.com. The Mets went 74-88 and finished in last place in 2026. The only silver lining to the disappointing season was the ability to give a long runway to rookies like Carson Benge and Nolan McLean, both of whom finished in the top four of the Rookie of the Year voting.

The Mets went 83-79 in 2025 and missed the postseason on the final day of the season. They made significant changes last winter, most notably jettisoning stalwarts Pete Alonso and Brandon Nimmo, then had a worse season in 2026. In September, president of baseball operations David Stearns admitted that much turnover created an "uncapped downside scenario," which is executive-speak for "there was too much risk."

Not surprisingly, the Braves are uninterested in moving former National League MVP Ronald Acuña Jr., according to MLB Network. It does feel like Atlanta's offense has gone stale and that they could move a core piece, but it won't be Acuña, nor is it likely to be Drake Baldwin, Michael Harris II, or Matt Olson. Ozzie Albies and Austin Riley are the more obvious players to move. Albies is entering the final season of his wildly team-friendly contract. Riley has six years remaining on his deal, which figures to make a move difficult.

On Monday, Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow declined to commit to Trevor Story as his starting shortstop next season. "We still have a ton of confidence in Trevor, but any decisions like that are going to take place between Trevor and me far before I speak to anything publicly," Breslow told reporters, including the Boston Globe. Boston has one of the top prospects in the minors in shortstop Franklin Arias, who is very likely to make his debut early next year. Arias could push Story into a utility role or off the team entirely.

#2615. Stephen Curry fires back at Gilbert Arenas, other podcasters for criticizing his wife Ayesha's on-screen kiss

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Roku Channel's new Christmas movie, Second Chance Holiday, premiered last Thursday, starring an actress in her first leading role: Ayesha Curry. The wife of Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has 20 acting credits on IMDB, but has never headlined a movie before, and with that new stature has come criticism.

Arenas claimed that Curry speaks to other men via direct messages on social media because "she needs the attention because he doesn't give her the attention because he's focused," alluding to previous comments Curry made about having "zero male attention."

Former NFL running back LeSean McCoy also cited that conversation in criticizing Curry. "This is crazy. You got one of the greatest players of all time as your husband," McCoy said on Speakeasy. "I've seen a while ago where she keeps saying how she wants more attention, and how girls throw themselves at him and she still just wants to feel like she's wanted… now you want us to see kissing a dude?… This is crazy."

On Wednesday, Stephen Curry addressed the comments with a video on Instagram.

"Nick, Gil, Emmanuel and anybody else who feels the need to jump in and give an opinion on something you don't really know about, something that kind of speaks to a bigger conversation on how you view women in this world and what they're allowed and what they're not allowed to do," Curry said. "Given the ignorance around how acting works, obviously I tried to laugh this one off but something needs to be said. Anytime Ayesha Curry shows up in your headline, kindly suggest that you just give the happy hands, the congratulations, and maybe the apology can be as loud as when y'all leading y'all shows with this topic."

Both Young, a former teammate of Curry's with the Warriors, and Arenas apologized Wednesday. "You my dog. I love you. If I said anything, I apologize like a man. I'm sorry," Young said.

"I'm sorry if he's offended; I didn't mean it like that. I was just saying, he's such a perfect dude," Arenas added, saying that Curry had never drawn controversy himself, but if someone in the family had, it was Ayesha.

NBA superstars are used to negativity from pundits, but commentary about their family is another matter. What Ayesha Curry does as an actress in a movie says nothing about her family or her husband's place in the basketball world. It's rare that Stephen Curry would address comments like this, but aside from the offense he and his family took, he was at least able to use it as a promotional opportunity.

"Appreciate the free pub, thank you for giving a nice shout-out to Second Chance Holiday," he said at the end of his video.

#2613. Drake Maye injury the latest for Patriots amid snakebitten 2026 Super Bowl hangover

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

A lot was made about the New England Patriots facing a historically easy schedule during their surprise run to Super Bowl LX in 2025. What flew more under the radar, however, was how remarkably healthy they were throughout that campaign. Between Week 1 and Super Bowl LX, New England placed just eight players on injured reserve. That's an astounding run of good health amid an NFL season, but water has found its level in 2026 in dramatic fashion.

The Patriots have been hit hard by injuries through 10 weeks of their 2026 season, and Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany may have delivered the kill shot.

At the tail end of the opening drive, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury that is reportedly feared to be season-ending. Specifically, there's concern the third-year quarterback may have fractured his ankle after taking a sack by pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson. Maye stayed in Germany for additional testing to see if surgery is required. He is already expected to miss a substantial period of time, possibly even the entire season.

That would be the death blow for a New England team already marred by injuries throughout 2026.

For instance, as noted by the Boston Herald, 16 of the Patriots' 22 Week 1 starters have either missed games or been knocked out of contests so far due to injury. That doesn't even include players like wideout Romeo Doubs, TreVeyon Henderson, and other rotational contributors.

For a broader view of just how much of a bit the injury bug has taken, here's a look at some notable Patriots who've missed time so far this season due to injury (courtesy of Pro Football Reference).

In total, 28 different players have been listed as out on gameday or placed on injured reserve heading into the Week 10 game in Germany, not including the loss of Maye that happened during that game. This is an entirely different circumstance than the health the team enjoyed last season, and it's adding up. New England now lost three of their last four games, moving to 5-5 entering the Week 11 bye.

Injuries reared their head almost instantly at the start of 2026. Most notably, A.J. Brown — the club's offseason prize acquired in a blockbuster trade with the Eagles — suffered a high ankle sprain in his Patriots debut. That landed him on injured reserve, keeping him out until Week 6. He missed two more games in Weeks 8 and 9, then left Sunday's contest early with a hamstring injury.

The hits have kept coming for Mike Vrabel's team, and they aren't limited to players who've missed games we highlighted above. There are plenty of Patriots who have been limited by injury, but still been able to suit up. Safety Kevin Byard (chest), left tackle Will Campbell (knee), linebacker Christian Elliss (chest), tight end Hunter Henry (foot), right tackle Morgan Moses (foot), running back Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), defensive back Charles Woods (shoulder, hamstring), and safety Craig Woodson (shoulder) have all popped up on the injury report throughout the season.

These are foundational pieces to what New England hoped would be a 2026 season that carried the momentum of last year's Super Bowl run and let them contend again. Instead, injuries — coupled with poor execution on the field — have turned a season once looked at with such promise upside down, especially in the wake of Maye's potential season-ender.

#2612. Blue Jays executive responds to Anthony Santander's 'extremely disappointing' anti-Muslim social media posts

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins had strong words Tuesday in reaction to Anthony Santander's anti-Muslim social media posts that he has since deleted.

"There really aren't words to express my level of disappointment," Atkins said from the GM meetings on Tuesday, via Sportsnet. "Anything exacerbating some level of hate, anti-Islamic, is just extremely concerning and extremely disappointing.

"I also talked to Anthony about his lack of awareness, realizing that he has a very large microphone, what that meant. We're working exceptionally hard internally to ensure, and we have been, that it's a safe environment, that baseball is for everyone. It's very important to us. It's a part of our organizational values and his behavior did not align with that."

Santander, a native Venezuelan, shared social media videos in the wake of the U.S. midterm elections last week, including one where a Christian pastor said, "there is no such thing as kind Muslims." Another implied that Sharia law would be imposed in the U.S. following the election of Abdul El-Sayed to the Senate. Santander has since taken down the videos from his social media pages.

In the aftermath, the team released the following statement:

"Baseball is for everyone, and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark. Individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs."

It's unclear whether Santander plans to address the matter publicly, but Atkins said he "told him that I thought he needed to and that he should."

As far as personal conversations with Santander, Atkins said, "I expressed my level of concern. I believe he felt it. I know he feels badly. But I don't want to speak for him."

Santander was signed as an amateur free agent out of Venezuela in 2011 when he was 16. He signed a free agent deal with the Blue Jays prior to the 2025 season; injuries have held him to just 54 games in the past two seasons.

#2611. Raptors Lose 15th Straight To Knicks: 4 Takeaways From Eastern Conference Thriller

Just two nights removed from their overtime loss on Sunday, the Toronto Raptors had a chance to set things right with a rematch against the New York Knicks. This time, to their credit, the Raptors came out firing with a 29-point first quarter that took the champs by surprise. By the end, however, it was the Knicks that overwhelmed, riding the play of their stars to win their second straight game (111-102) and 15th straight against the Raptors in particular.

As usual, Jalen Brunson led the way for New York. In 34 minutes, he finished with 31 points, five rebounds, five assists, zero steals, and one block on 45.5% shooting from the field (4-11 from three). At shooting guard, Mikal Bridges dropped 17 points, five rebounds, and one assist on 63.6% shooting from the field (2-5 from three), while center Karl-Anthony Towns dropped 16 points, 16 rebounds, eight assists, and one steal on 77.8% shooting from the field (1-2 from three).

For the Raptors, Ja'Kobe Walter led the way with 25 points, one rebound, two assists, and two steals on 60.0% shooting from the field (7-12 from three). Veteran swingman RJ Barrett, meanwhile, contributed 22 points, five rebounds, five assists, zero steals, and one block on 52.9% shooting from the field (2-8 from three). Finally, there's Scottie Barnes: 20 points, four rebounds, two assists, and two blocks on 50.0% shooting (1-2 from three).

Whether it was the support of their home crowd or the desperation of not wanting to lose to the same team in back-to-back games, the Raptors came out with a lot of energy in this game, playing with an almost desperate urgency during the early minutes of the game. Eventually, though, that urgency turned to frustration as the Knicks got increasingly comfortable and expanded their lead down the stretch.

In the grand scheme of things, this game likely won't be remembered for long, but it told us a lot about where these teams are headed going into the holiday season (NBA Christmas and Cup Finals). For the Knicks especially, it's a step in the right direction that could signal an upcoming shift in the hierarchy.

To say Mikal Bridges was struggling this season would be an understatement. He looked borderline unplayable at times, and head coach Mike Brown was facing growing calls to bench him. He started showing signs of life against the Pacers on Friday (18 points in 28 minutes), and he showed a familiar spark in today's win, finishing with 17 points, five rebounds, and one assist on 63.6% shooting from the field and 40.0% shooting from three. Bridges held a steady rhythm all game, and that's when the Knicks are at their best.

Of course, even when Bridges was at his worst offensively, he still made a positive impact on defense. Tonight, that defensive touch was massive in containing the Raptors' shooting and regularly contesting their attempts. Bridges was active on this end throughout the game, making that quiet impact even when he wasn't scoring.

It's unclear what had Bridges in such a funk to begin with, but everything is easier for the Knicks when he's making shots. By easing pressure off Brunson, spacing the floor, and punishing teams for leaving him open, it answers so many problems, and we saw how it worked out for them against the Raptors.

If there's one specific time when the Knicks are prone to elevate their game, it's the fourth quarter. Tonight, after stumbling through most of the first half, they sealed the deal with a 31-point fourth quarter that ultimately decided the game. New York's best moments came in the final three minutes, when Brunson single-handedly willed his team to victory after making a four-point play to put them up by four. Even Mikal got in on the action, delivering a dagger three with roughly 45 seconds left.

The Knicks started the season 1-6 in clutch games, but we can assume that was an outlier now. As we were reminded today, this team is loaded with players who are not afraid of the moment. When the pressure was highest, they played with a sense of calm and poise, leading to smart decisions and crisp passes that always found their man. At this point, the Knicks have seen it all together, and they aren't fazed by the pressure.

What makes the Knicks so hard to beat is that they only get better in the clutch, and it's not just Brunson who beats you. Tonight, practically everyone had their moment, highlighting the depth and versatility of the defending champions.

As Kawhi Leonard deals with swelling in his left knee, his status remains a mystery, leaving the Raptors without their best player. They clearly missed him tonight, but how much will his return actually change for this team? Other than Scottie Barnes and RJ Barrett, the Raptors don't have nearly enough depth or talent to keep up with the likes of the 76ers, Celtics, or Pistons in the East. They traded away their best perimeter scorer (Brandon Ingram) and gave up a promising young athlete in Gradey Dick.

What the Raptors really lack is a center. Jakob Poeltl came off the bench tonight in favor of Collin Murray-Boyles, who finished with just eight points, one rebound, three assists, one steal, and three blocks on 66.7% shooting from the field. Sensing their advantage in the frontcourt, the Knicks were feasting inside, going in for easy layups and controlling the glass for a 44-23 rebounding advantage.

While there's no doubt the Raptors will be better off for Kawhi's return, they cannot rely on him to come back and just resolve their issues. To salvage this season, more proactive measures are required, and the options are limitless.

The Knicks' bench was a cause for concern going into the season, and it didn't build confidence when their best bench scorer from last season (Jordan Clarkson) started seeing reduced minutes. Fortunately, veteran Landry Shamet has been filling the role just fine, and he gave the Knicks another fine showing tonight. In 24 minutes off the bench, he put up 12 points, one rebound, and one assist on 57.1% shooting from the field (2-4 from three).

As the Raptors struggled to get anything from their second unit, Landry Shamet carried the Knicks' bench to ensure his team never lost momentum. His versatility let him fit into various lineups, and he made few mistakes while providing a steady boost on the court. So while Shamet may not be the hero Knicks fans were expecting, he's becoming a big storyline for their turnaround this season, and his importance is undeniable.

Ultimately, the Knicks will always lean more on their star-studded starting lineup, but having that boost off the bench makes everything easier. Tonight, we saw the impact Shamet could have (+26) and why we can expect to see more of him over the course of the season.

#2607. 2026 MLB Manager of the Year: White Sox's Will Venable, Brewers' Pat Murphy win BBWAA awards

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Chicago White Sox manager Will Venable and Brewers manager Pat Murphy were named the Managers of the Year in their respective leagues on Tuesday night as part of the BBWAA's awards week. Murphy is the first manager to ever win the award in three consecutive seasons.

The annual awards, which also include Manager of the Year, Reliever of the Year, Cy Young and MVP, are voted on by 30 members of the Baseball Writers Association of America (that's two per MLB city in each league). Votes were submitted before the beginning of the playoffs, meaning that only regular-season contributions are taken into account.

Murphy, manager of the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, has been voted the National League Manager of the Year, the Baseball Writers Association of America announced on Tuesday. He is the first person to win three consecutive Manager of the Year awards and the tenth person with three Manager of the Year wins in total.

Ballots for the BBWAA's awards are submitted between the end of the regular season and the beginning of the postseason. They are regular-season awards and Milwaukee's World Series win did not factor into the voting.

Of course, Murphy did not need the World Series win to boost his Manager of the Year case. He guided the small-market Brewers to baseball's best record (103-59) and run differential (+214) during the regular season, and their fourth consecutive NL Central title. Their 103 wins are a franchise record and baseball's most since 2023.

Murphy just completed his third season as Brewers manager and has three Manager of the Year wins to show for it. Bobby Cox (2004-05), Kevin Cash (2020-21), and Stephen Vogt (2024-25) are the only others with two consecutive Manager of the Year awards. Vogt was not an American League Manager of the Year finalist this season.

Prior to Murphy's threepeat here, the Brewers had never had a Manager of the Year winner. He's won the award now three times in three years at the helm.

Atlanta Braves manager Walt Weiss and Philadelphia Phillies manager Don Mattingly finished behind Murphy in the voting. Mattingly took over as an interim after the Phillies fired Rob Thomson on April 28. Philadelphia had baseball's fourth-best record after the managerial change. Weiss guided the Braves to the NL East title.

Venable, who helped orchestrate a 24-win year-to-year improvement and guided the team to its first postseason berth since 2021, has been named the American League Manager of the Year, the Baseball Writers Association of America announced on Tuesday. He beat out Tampa Bay Rays manager Kevin Cash and Boston Red Sox manager Chad Tracy.

The White Sox went 84-78 in 2026 after going 60-102 in 2025 and a hideous 41-121 in 2024. Those 121 losses are the record in baseball's Modern Era (since 1900). Venable's White Sox are the first team in history to reach the postseason after losing at least 100 games in the previous two seasons (they also lost 101 games in 2023).

The huge steps forward seem to be what secured the award for Venable. He took over in 2025 and the White Sox improved by 19 wins that season, only to turn around and improve by 24 more wins this past season. They were arguably the most surprising playoff team in 2026 and Venable gets his due here.

Venable joins the following White Sox manager of the year winners:

Cash finishes as the runner-up in a very close vote. Venable got 15 of the 30 first-place votes while Cash got 12. Tracy finishes in third place, with Guardians manager Stephen Vogt fourth and Yankees' skipper Aaron Boone sitting fifth.

Cash's Rays improved by 21 games to win an AL-best 98 and win the AL East after finishing in fourth place in 2025. Tracy took over the Red Sox after Alex Cora started 10-17 and was fired. Tracy went 77-58 and earned the second AL wild card.

#2605. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2603. Joe Burrow isn't just chasing MVP, he's chasing the greatest passing season ever

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Two years ago, Joe Burrow resigned himself to the fact that, despite having an MVP-caliber season, he likely wouldn't win the award based on the Bengals' 9-8 record and absence from the playoffs.

"I'll win one one day," Burrow said at the time.

Already the MVP favorite entering Sunday night's game against the Steelers, Burrow is now the clear front-runner. Against a team that defeated the Bengals back in Week 3, Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns while completing nearly 80% of his passes. It could have been much more, but Bengals coach Zac Taylor called off the dogs and took Burrow out of the game midway through the fourth quarter of Cincinnati's eventual 38-18 win.

Playing in the background of Burrow's performance were MVP chants from Bengals fans, which Taylor acknowledged hearing throughout the game. Taylor, as you'd expect, agrees with that sentiment.

"I mean it would be impossible to say that anyone is playing better," Taylor said. "I'm not watching every game ... but I bet the people that aren't talking about him aren't watching our games, because if you are, it's really hard to say that he is not the best player on planet Earth."

Burrow's performance not only strengthened his MVP case but also put him on a historic trajectory with eight games to play in the 2026 regular season.

Burrow is one of only five quarterbacks in NFL history with over 30 total touchdowns through nine games, according to CBS Sports Research. The other four won league MVP: Tom Brady in 2007, Aaron Rodgers in 2011, Peyton Manning in 2013 and Patrick Mahomes in 2018.

Burrow joined Manning on Sunday night as the only two quarterbacks with five consecutive games with at least four touchdowns. Over that span, Burrow has thrown 20 touchdowns (against just three interceptions) and ran for two more while completing 78% of his passes. The Bengals won each of those games while taking sole possession of first place in the AFC North.

Burrow is on pace to become the third quarterback to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season. He is on pace to throw 51 touchdown passes, which would put him behind Manning's 55 during the 2013 season. Burrow's 5,279 yards would rank fourth behind Manning (5,477 in 2013), Drew Brees (5,476 in 2011) and Brady (5,316 in 2021).

While he's not on pace to break those records, Burrow is on track to create his own category for quarterback excellence by becoming the first quarterback to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season while also completing 70% of his passes. If he does that, he will have a strong argument when it comes to having the greatest passing season in league history.

Burrow's success can be attributed to his growth as well as improvements across Cincinnati's entire roster. The Bengals' offensive line has improved, and the defense has greatly benefited from the offseason acquisitions of Dexter Lawrence, Boye Mafe and Bryan Cook. It goes without saying that the trio of running back Chase Brown and wideouts Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have helped, too.

Now in his fourth season, Brown has established himself as one of the league's more versatile running backs. He had two touchdown catches on Sunday night and was second on the team with eight receptions.

"We know what we have in Chase," Burrow said. "He's a big-time playmaker for us. When people devote too many resources to stopping the guys on the outside, Chase can beat you in a lot of different ways."

That's now two TDs for Chase Brown and FOUR TDs for Joe Burrow 😎PITvsCIN on NBC/PeacockStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/svZHSPGVmC

Chase and Higgins are the league's best receiving duo and have been for some time. They're on pace to become the first pair of teammates to each post 1,500-yard receiving seasons in the same year.

Higgins is on pace to record a career-high 1,556 receiving yards this season, while Chase (who actually trailed Higgins in receiving yards prior to Sunday night) is on pace to have 1,658 receiving yards this season after catching 11 passes for 231 yards against Pittsburgh.

Joe Burrow throws it deep to Ja'Marr Chase for the first down 🚀PITvsCIN on NBC/PeacockStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o97edw3OV3

Looking ahead, the Bengals have only three remaining games against teams with winning records (Cleveland in Weeks 13 and 18, the Chiefs in Week 14). The Browns have given Burrow fits in the past, but Myles Garrett (now a Ram) was a big reason for that. Burrow has historically played well against the Chiefs.

As Burrow alluded to in his postgame press conference, it's only mid-November with a lot of football left to play. That may be true, but it is also true that Burrow has put himself -- and his team -- in position to have a memorable, and perhaps historic, season.

#2602. Astros name franchise icon Brad Ausmus as new manager as Houston tries to turn back the clock

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Houston Astros have chosen Brad Ausmus as their next manager, the team announced on Wednesday

Ausmus replaces Joe Espada, whose contract as Houston manager was not renewed after three seasons. Espada led the Astros to the playoffs in two of those seasons.

"I am very excited to be back in Houston," Ausmus said in a statement. "The Astros and the city of Houston have been a huge part of my life, and I'm thrilled to create a new chapter as the team's manager. I'd like to thank [general manager Randy Flores] and the entire Astros organization for this opportunity, and I can't wait to get to work."

Ausmus, 57, had served as bench coach for the New York Yankees since late 2023. Prior to that, he had two stints as a big-league manager. He first managed the Detroit Tigers from 2014-17, and over that span he guided the team to a 314-332 record and a division title in his first season. Ausmus also managed the Angels to a 72-90 record in 2019. Overall, Ausmus as a manager has a winning percentage of .478 in five seasons.

Before his dugout career, Ausmus was a top defensive catcher for years. Ausmus's playing career spanned parts of 18 seasons in Major League Baseball, 10 of which came with the Astros. Along the way, Ausmus won three Gold Gloves behind the mask and earned an All-Star selection as a member of the Tigers in 1999.

"We are thrilled to welcome Brad back to the Astros organization," Flores said in a statement. "Brad impressed us throughout the interview process, demonstrating the leadership, energy, and expertise critical to driving a winning culture both on and off the field. I am excited to work alongside Brad and happy to have him back in an Astros uniform."

With Houston, Ausmus is the first major hire undertaken by Flores, who himself was named to his post earlier in the offseason. The Astros are coming off a division title and a postseason berth in 2026. However, they also finished 81-81 and had a negative run differential. It's an uncertain future, as the Astros have an aging roster in spots, a weak farm system, and multiple core contributors entering their walk years in 2027.

It remains to be seen whether owner Jim Crane will try to wring out another season of contention from the roster or lean into a rebuild. Whatever the course, Ausmus will help guide it in a city where he remains a highly popular figure.

As of Houston's decision to hire Ausmus, the Los Angeles Angels are the only team with a current managerial vacancy. Earlier in the offseason, the Philadelphia Phillies retained interim manager Don Mattingly on a permanent basis, as did the New York Mets with Andy Green, and the Seattle Mariners replaced Dan Wilson with Jason Kanzler.

#2599. Sean Payton disputes Jim Harbaugh's 'loophole' claim after Broncos-Chargers trade falls apart

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

At the trade deadline last Tuesday, a rare inter-division deal was agreed to between the Los Angeles Chargers and Denver Broncos. The Broncos agreed to send the Chargers a fourth-round pick and a future fifth-round pick in exchange for linebacker Daiyan Henley, but the deal fell apart.

The trade was nixed after Denver reportedly found an issue with Henley's knee during his physical. ESPN reported that the Broncos then approached the Chargers and attempted to renegotiate the compensation. Denver still wanted to acquire the linebacker, but just not at the price George Paton and Sean Payton initially agreed to.

Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters last Thursday that the Broncos backing out of the deal sets a bad precedent, and that this is a "loophole" the NFL needs to investigate.

"That's why it's a loophole, and teams should not have the ability to do that," Harbaugh said. "It's a medical grade. It's a pass/fail for a medical trade. They told us they weren't going to pass him if there was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon. They would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a 'fill in the blank.' I don't know what to call that, but that's what it is."

The Broncos were on a bye in Week 10, so we had to wait until Monday to hear their side of the story. Payton was indeed asked about the trade falling through, but didn't offer many details.

"I'm not going to get into the specifics. He's prospect we thought of — and still do — very highly of. It just didn't work out," Payton said, via The Athletic. "I'll leave it at that."

What did Payton think about Harbaugh's comments regarding a "loophole?"

"Listen, I thought I saw it all," he said, via Mile High Sports. "There's no loophole. It's just part of the trade process, every step of the way."

Whatever the Broncos found in Henley's knee hasn't affected him yet. He hasn't missed a game due to injury in each of the last two seasons. In eight games played this season, Henley has recorded 51 tackles, half a sack, two passes defensed and an interception. The Broncos and Chargers will see each other again in the regular-season finale when Week 18 rolls around.

#2598. Victor Wembanyama’s ridiculous self-assisted dunk steals the show despite Spurs’ 105-93 loss to Pistons

Victor Wembanyama produced another highlight-reel moment against the Detroit Pistons, throwing the ball off the backboard before catching it and finishing with a one-handed dunk.

The San Antonio Spurs star used his incredible height and creativity to get past Ausar Thompson early in their meeting with Detroit.

Wembanyama had already been blocked by one of the Thompson twins this season, but he found a different way to attack the basket this time.

The 22-year-old drove towards the paint just over a minute into the game before sensing pressure from Thompson. Rather than force his way through the defence, Wembanyama threw the ball against the backboard, collected it in the air and threw down a one-handed finish.

It was a reminder of the unusual skills that make the Frenchman such a difficult player to defend. At 7-foot-4, Wembanyama has the size to dominate near the rim, but his ability to improvise makes him even more dangerous.

He entered the contest averaging 28.6 points and 11.6 rebounds through 14 appearances, ranking third and fifth in the NBA in those categories respectively.

However, the highlight did not tell the full story of the night for San Antonio.

Despite Wembanyama finishing with 25 points and 18 rebounds, the Spurs fell to a 105-93 defeat against Detroit at the Frost Bank Center. Dylan Harper added 20 points, while Julian Champagnie scored 14.

Detroit also had the final say in the battle of the big moments, with Cade Cunningham producing a poster dunk over Wembanyama near the end of the first quarter.

The defeat leaves San Antonio with a 12-3 record after starting the season strongly.
